name: glastig

attributes.attribute: a gray thin fairy, meaning the gray-handed one
had long yellow hair that reached the ground behind her
wore green, leading to the name green glastig

sources: MacKenzie, Donald A. Scottish Folk-Lore and Folk Life: Studies in Race, Culture and Tradition. Glasgow: Blackie & Sons, Ltd., 1935, pp. 176–194.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The glastig is a Scottish and Welsh fairy. Her name means the gray-handed one. She was a gray thin woman, sometimes a giant. Her long yellow hair reached the ground behind her. She wore the fairy green, so some called her the green glastig. She rarely appeared in company, though a pair was sometimes seen. Glastig hung around farms with cows. She also loved friendly people of low intelligence and cared for them. Her voice was preternaturally loud and carried for miles. As a spirit of milk cattle, she demanded the first milk each morning. A stingy dairyman lost his milk, which she dried up as punishment. Regular libations of milk set on the doorstep kept her near. Like the brownie, she cleaned well when guests were coming. People never spoke of her or praised her labor, for then she moved to another farm.
